scope: Scrape video and link Copy in the owned native side panel
current_verdict: Product Copy outcome remains unverified; the receipts prove trusted clicks and an opaque clipboard read failure, not a failed clipboard write.
evidence: Native run 37222954472 records four trusted scrape-media-copy clicks (video and link, warm and reload), zero pointer failures, and four clipboard_url=null / copy_unavailable:panel_runtime_exception results. Run 37221586281 records the same pattern for two warm clicks.

tests/browser/scrape-native-media-actions.mjs calls evaluate(panel, 'navigator.clipboard.readText()') after each Copy click. It neither observes the CopyButton success/failure icon nor inspects clipboard read rejection details.

tests/browser/settings-panel-driver.mjs converts every Runtime.evaluate exceptionDetails result to the same panel_runtime_exception string. Consequently the receipt cannot distinguish NotAllowedError, focus/visibility denial, missing clipboard API, or an unrelated JavaScript exception.

src/features/scrape/ScrapeView.tsx renders both controls through CopyButton. src/components/CopyMenu.tsx changes the icon to emerald Check only when copyToClipboard returns true, or red X when it returns false. The native Scrape receipt does not capture either state.

EXT-D-0027 already established that a focused, visible extension panel can reject clipboard-read with NotAllowedError; tests/browser/clipboard-observation.mjs provides scoped Browser.setPermission for owned-origin readback and restores the prior permission. The reviewed Debug .90 native run observed Copy feedback, exact readback, and restoration. Scrape does not call that helper.
causal_boundary: The first proven loss of diagnostic information is the Scrape harness's direct clipboard read through settings-panel-driver evaluate. The real product write result is upstream and was not observed.
one_run_discriminator: For each trusted Copy click, sample the same button's emerald Check versus red X within its 1.2-second feedback window; classify product write feedback independently of clipboard readback.

Self-catch navigator.clipboard.readText rejection inside Runtime.evaluate and return only an allowlisted error name plus document.hasFocus() and visibilityState, never the clipboard content or raw exception in the receipt.

If feedback is Check and read rejects NotAllowedError while focused/visible, use the existing D27 withClipboardReadPermission only after the click, with an owned browser CDP session and prior-permission restoration. Compare the returned value with the fixture URL in memory and record only equality. A red X is a product failure regardless of read permission; no icon is an unresolved timing/observation failure.
source_change: None: a browser/native run is excluded from this lane, so no real error class or product feedback is available to justify a behavioral patch. Reuse the existing D27 observer in the next owned run; do not add a second permission mechanism.
